bullets: What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?
Don’t expect huge reversals right away, but we could see more support for renewables.
I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night.

And it didn’t take long to see the beginning of the blue wave: Democrats took control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, a dramatic swing from Donald Trump’s victory two years ago.
While the results are striking, we probably won’t be seeing some of the big climate and energy policy shifts that have come in recent years as Congress and the presidency have changed hands.

posts.title: AI on the Ballot
posts.summary: Data Centers were on the ballot, and they lost in a major way; what does it mean if American opposition to building is permanent?
bullets: The 2026 midterm elections saw a significant political backlash against data center expansion, with both major parties utilizing anti-data center rhetoric as a key campaign strategy.

Texas, which holds over 25% of projected U.S. data center capacity through 2030, has become a focal point for regulatory risk following the election of a governor who pledged a construction moratorium.
The shift in political sentiment represents a reversal from the historical trend where local governments actively competed for data center investments due to tax and economic benefits.

The current wave of opposition is uniquely tied to AI infrastructure, signaling that the massive energy and resource requirements of AI models are now a primary driver of legislative and electoral friction.

posts.title: China October NEV retail sales fall 10% to 1.148 million, preliminary CPCA data shows
posts.summary:
October passenger NEV retail sales rose 6% from a month earlier, pushing the penetration rate to a record high of 67.8%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's passenger NEV retail sales reached 1.148 million units in October, a 10% year-on-year decline, though sales increased 6% month-on-month.

The NEV retail penetration rate hit a record high of 67.8%, signaling that electric vehicles continue to capture market share despite a broader 25% year-on-year slump in total passenger car retail sales.
Cumulative NEV retail sales for the first 10 months of 2026 fell 12% to 8.907 million units, reflecting ongoing challenges in the Chinese automotive market.
The CPCA noted that a lack of 'blockbuster' models and high operating costs for internal combustion engine vehicles are driving the current market dynamics.
